name: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash

sources.note: aggregator mirror of the Artificial Analysis Coding Index, read 2026-11-19; no per-row dates; upstream AA pages not reachable

purpose: MiniMax states: a native multimodal MoE model for coding, agentic workflows, computer use and cybersecurity, with text, image and video input and up to 1 M tokens of context.

lineage.how_derived: M3 decoder geometry kept; first three full-attention layers replaced by sparse attention; quantization-aware training of routed experts and attention paths; DSpark draft head instead of the earlier MTP

license.name: MiniMax Community License (minimax-community)
license.notes: LICENSE read. Grant is "for non-commercial purposes". Commercial Use needs (1) the notice "Built with MiniMax M3.1-Flash" and (2) a one-time notice to MiniMax, or a prior written authorization when the product earns more than USD 20 million a year. "Commercial Use" includes offering products or services for a fee and deploying fine-tuned or modified weights for any commercial purpose. Appendix of prohibited uses includes any military purpose. Not an open-source license. Verdict policy (README, 2026-11-19): this licence term does not lower tona_fit; kept here for an installer label.

architecture.attention: MiniMax Sparse Attention on every layer (64 heads, 4 KV heads)
architecture.drafter: DSpark draft head (separate file dspark/, GGUF dspark-...Q8_0 2.1 GB in the unsloth repo)
architecture.why_this_design: MiniMax states: sparse attention throughout, quantization-aware training and DSpark speculative decoding improve inference efficiency; DSpark replaces the earlier EAGLE-like MTP approach.

pc-12gb.notes: estimate from the file size (129.4 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 60 GB; about 7% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

pc-16gb.notes: estimate from the file size (129.4 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 13.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 64 GB; about 11% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that)

engine_support.notes: GGUFs exist (unsloth, 2026-10-23); a Blackwell-only C++/CUDA engine reports 17 tok/s decode on a single RTX 5090 (HF discussion 14). Tona would need a new module (MSA with indexer, 128 experts, DSpark).

strengths: Vendor table puts it level with GPT-5.6 Sol on DeepSWE v1.1 (73.7 against 73.0) and above GLM-5.3 (66.9)
long-running tasks with good memory and focus (one user report)
weaknesses: Smallest quant is 129 GB: only 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class machines can hold it
Commercial use carries notice and attribution duties; above USD 20 M revenue written authorization
No independent score found (not in the Artificial Analysis Coding Index mirror, only MiniMax M3 at 58.6)
soft.behavior: reasoning_effort low / medium / high / xhigh / max; recommended temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95.
best_for: long-running agentic coding on large unified-memory or 128 GB RAM machines
avoid_for: users who cannot meet the commercial notice terms
soft.maturity: MiniMax: established vendor (M2.x, M3); 110k downloads of the main repo, 15 discussions.

user_reports.summary: Positive long-task impression: good memory, good focus, "underrated" next to DeepSeek and GLM recent models
Blackwell-only C++/CUDA engine runs it at 17 tok/s decode on one RTX 5090; a reader calls that unusable for agentic coding

tona_fit.reason: Vendor agent numbers are strong, but the smallest GGUF (129 GB) fits only the 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM class marginally and there is no independent evidence. Revisit with an independent coding score or a smaller quant.
blockers: Tona has no module for MiniMax Sparse Attention and DSpark (engine support, not a quality judgement)

open_questions: Independent coding score: not found. Check: Artificial Analysis page for the model, SWE-bench / DeepSWE leaderboards after release.
Quality of UD-IQ1_M on code. Check: our own polyglot run on the quant.
